findings.description: An AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block, committed to source control and stored in Terraform state; anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or state file access can retrieve them.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which here hold long-lived AWS credentials) are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are decrypted and displayed to any principal able to read the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with a restricted key policy would enforce separate authorization for secret access.
The function runs nodejs12.x, an end-of-life Lambda runtime that no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known runtime vulnerabilities unpatched.

The function declares no vpc_config, so it executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the code is compromised.

The assume-role policy trusts lambda.amazonaws.com with no aws:SourceArn or aws:SourceAccount condition, so the trust relationship is not scoped to a specific function or account, leaving a confused-deputy path broader than necessary.
